h1: How a Private Engineering College Can Get 2.5x More Admissions in One Season
quickAnswer: In this benchmark scenario, a private engineering college spending ₹12 lakh across a four-month admission season runs programme-level ads, qualifying lead forms and a WhatsApp nurture sequence aimed at students and parents. Admissions from digital rise from 48 to 122, and cost per admission falls from ₹25,000 to ₹9,836.
cardSummary: 2.5x more admissions from digital in one season, with cost per admission down from ₹25,000 to under ₹10,000.

businessPattern.type: Single campus, 6 UG and PG programmes, state-level intake
businessPattern.location: Metro outskirts; students from across the state and neighbouring states
businessPattern.salesCycle: 2–6 months, decided jointly by student and parents
businessPattern.seasonAdBudget: ₹12 lakh over 4 months (₹3 lakh/month, Google + Meta + YouTube)

challenge: "We get thousands of form fills, but counsellors waste days calling students who only wanted the brochure." Leads came from broad Meta campaigns with no programme or rank filter. Counsellors had no priority order, and follow-up stopped after two unanswered calls.
objectives: Lower cost per admission by at least 40% within the season
Lift lead-to-application rate by improving lead quality

whatWeDid.title: Programme-level campaigns
whatWeDid.body: Separate Google Search and Meta campaigns for each programme, with landing pages showing fees, placements, scholarships and cut-off ranks.

whatWeDid.title: Qualifying lead forms
whatWeDid.body: Forms asked entrance rank range, programme and city, so counsellors called the best-fit leads first.

whatWeDid.title: Parent-focused creative
whatWeDid.body: YouTube and Facebook videos covering safety, hostels, faculty and placement support, targeted at parents aged 40–55.

whatWeDid.title: WhatsApp nurture sequence
whatWeDid.body: Every lead received programme details, campus-tour slots and counselling dates over four weeks. Counsellors worked a ranked daily list.

whatWeDid.title: Campus-visit push
whatWeDid.body: Weekend open-house invites by WhatsApp and retargeting — the stage where most applications were made.

whatMadeTheDifference: Treating admissions as a funnel, not a lead count. Qualifying questions and a ranked call list let counsellors spend their time on students likely to join, and the WhatsApp sequence kept the college in front of parents through a decision that takes months.

faqs.question: How can a college get more admissions through digital marketing?
faqs.answer: Run separate campaigns for each programme, send traffic to pages that show fees, placements and cut-offs, qualify leads on the form, and nurture them on WhatsApp until campus visits and counselling.

faqs.question: What is a good cost per lead for education ads in India?
faqs.answer: Published Indian benchmarks put education Meta cost per lead at roughly ₹200–450. Cost per admission is the number that matters.

faqs.question: Should admission ads target parents?
faqs.answer: Yes. Parents influence or decide most UG choices. Videos on safety, hostels, faculty and placements work well on YouTube and Facebook for ages 40–55.

faqs.question: When should an admission campaign start?
faqs.answer: Start awareness 2–3 months before entrance results and scale lead generation from results week through counselling rounds.
